title: Further differentiation rules

points.text: Derivatives of x^n, sin x, cos x, e^x and ln x

bigPicture: Five standard derivatives and three rules (chain, product, quotient) let you differentiate any function in the course. Spot the structure first, then apply the rule.

keyIdeas.answer: x^n → nx^(n−1); sin x → cos x; cos x → −sin x; e^x → e^x; ln x → 1/x.
Differentiate term by term; constants multiply through: (kf)′ = kf′.
For y = f(g(x)): dy/dx = f′(g(x)) × g′(x), i.e. dy/du × du/dx. Example: e^(3x) → 3e^(3x); sin(x²) → 2x cos(x²).

keyTerms.def: a function of a function, f(g(x))
g(x) in f(g(x)); its derivative multiplies the result

misconceptions.right: It is vu′ − uv′: the order matters.

practice.prompt: f(x) = e^(2x) cos x. Find f′(x) and the gradient of the curve at x = 1.
solution: f′(x) = 2e^(2x) cos x − e^(2x) sin x

assessmentNote: AA SL external exams: Paper 1 without a calculator and Paper 2 with a GDC, both written answers in sections A (short) and B (extended); no multiple choice. Practice prompts here are original and are not predictions of exam questions.
